title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Validation and Cutover
purpose: Describe the bounded runtime path that validates a chosen preferred address before migration, answers PATH_CHALLENGE on that preferred-address candidate path, and sends later non-probing packets only from the validated preferred address.
design_summary: Preferred-address traffic is modeled as an address-change candidate path whose remote address and port match either advertised preferred IPv4 or IPv6 endpoint. The existing path-change handler creates a candidate path and sends a PATH_CHALLENGE rather than promoting the address immediately. PATH_CHALLENGE frames carried in protected 1-RTT packets on that candidate path are parsed by the application-data frame loop and answered with a matching PATH_RESPONSE on the same path. Once path validation succeeds, the single-active-path runtime promotes the validated preferred-address path, records the previous path as the preferred-address migration source, and subsequent non-probing sends such as close frames use only the promoted preferred-address path.
data_and_state_considerations: Candidate-path validation state, anti-amplification budget, and recently validated path records remain in the runtime path tables. Preferred-address matching compares parsed IP bytes and ports against the committed peer transport-parameter snapshot. The preferred-address connection ID remains under peer connection-ID state or the existing preferred-address fallback and is not expanded into a public migration API in this slice.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A preferred-address candidate remains unpromoted until path validation succeeds.
A PATH_CHALLENGE received on the preferred-address candidate path receives a matching PATH_RESPONSE on that same path without promoting the path.
Both advertised IPv4 and IPv6 preferred addresses are eligible chosen preferred-address paths when their address bytes and port match the committed transport parameter.
After validation, non-probing sends are emitted only on the chosen preferred-address path and not on the original path.
The proof uses the current single-active-path runtime and does not claim simultaneous multipath operation.
alternatives_considered: Promote the preferred address as soon as any datagram is observed; rejected because the requirement requires validation before migration.
Treat the PATH_CHALLENGE response proof as covered only by generic Section 8.2 tests; rejected because S9P6P2 needs direct preferred-address candidate-path evidence.
Broaden the slice into complete preferred-address transition closure; rejected because S9P6P2 has additional address-source and abandonment tails that should stay independently traceable.
risks: The proof stays at the runtime transition seam and does not claim hosted endpoint interop success.
The current runtime promotes on the path-validation success event; future work that models the explicit largest-packet-number gate must preserve these preferred-address non-probing send guarantees.
The slice does not close the remaining S9P6P2 preferred-address requirements outside 0008 through 0010.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers preferred-address validation, PATH_CHALLENGE response, and validated IPv4/IPv6 non-probing cutover for the current single-active-path runtime only.
